title: Zileuton for Food Allergy
official: Investigation of Zileuton as a Novel Treatment to Prevent Anaphylaxis for Children and Adolescents With Food Allergies
summary:
Our proposed project will seek to determine if an oral medication called zileuton, which blocks the synthesis of inflammatory molecules called leukotrienes that are involved in allergic reactions, may be able to decrease absorption of food allergens and prevent severe food allergy reactions from occurring. Our study will measure levels of peanut in the blood before and after subjects consume an allergen they can tolerate and compare the results with and without administration of the study medication, zileuton. If our study shows that zileuton can decrease the absorption of a food allergen, this will allow us to see if this medication can be used to prevent anaphylaxis to food.

The goal of this proof-of-concept study is to determine whether zileuton inhibits food allergen absorption in children and adolescents with food allergy. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does zileuton administration impact food allergen absorption in children and adolescents with food allergies?
* What is the variability of food allergen absorption in children and adolescents with IgE-mediated food allergies?

Researchers will compare levels of peanut allergen proteins in the participants' blood with and without a dose of zileuton prior to a test meal of peanut protein.

* Visit 1 will involve a baseline blood draw, a test meal of peanut protein and a post-meal blood draw.
* Visit 2 will involve a baseline blood draw, a dose of zileuton before the test meal of peanut protein, and blood draws after the test meal.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adolescent subjects ages 12-17
* Parent or guardian fluent in English
* Known IgE-mediated food allergy other than peanut

  * Confirmed by clinical history of reaction to the food antigen plus

    1. positive skin prick testing and/or serum food-specific IgE AND
    2. confirmation of the food allergy diagnosis by a board-certified allergist

Exclusion Criteria:

* A previous positive peanut specific IgE test or skin prick test, or a history of any allergic symptoms following peanut consumption
* Medical conditions known to affect the gastrointestinal tract
* Any history of hepatic disease or previous abnormal liver function tests
* Previous hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis to zileuton
* Current use of a medication known to interact with zileuton, such as theophylline, warfarin, or propranolol
* History of drug or alcohol abuse
* Use of any investigational drugs within 30 days of screening
* Initiation of allergen immunotherapy within 3 months prior to Visit 1 or a plan to begin therapy during the trial
* Use of leukotriene antagonists/modifier such as montelukast
* Pregnant persons
* Individuals with uncontrolled neuropsychiatric disorders
* Use of oral corticosteroids (OCS) within 2 weeks before screening or are scheduled to receive OCS during the study period for another condition
* Monoclonal antibody or immunosuppressive treatment within 3 months of screening
* Past or current medical problems which in the opinion of the investigator, may pose additional risks from participation in the study, may interfere with the participant's ability to comply with study requirements or may compromise the quality of the data obtained from the study
* Inability or unwillingness of a parent or guardian to give written informed consent or participant to give assent
* Non-English speaking participants
